title: Charging by rubbing: how electrons jump from hair to a balloon
examples: How does rubbing a balloon make it charged?
Why does my hair stand up after rubbing a balloon?

explain.say: Rub a balloon on your hair, then lift it slowly. Your hair rises up to follow it, as if by magic! It is not magic. It is static electricity, which means electric charge that builds up and stays put. Let us see it happen.

explain.say: Look at the second stage. Everything is made of atoms, and atoms have tiny electrons with a negative charge. When you rub, some electrons jump from your hair onto the balloon. Only electrons move. Which way do they jump?

explain.say: From hair to balloon, yes! Now see the third stage: the balloon has extra electrons, so it is negative. And the fourth: your hair has lost some, so it is positive. Positive and negative are the two kinds of charge. Which one is negative?

explain.say: The balloon! Now look at the last stage: opposite charges attract, so your positive hair is pulled to the negative balloon. But like charges repel, which means push apart. So why do your hairs spread out from each other?

explain.say: Because each hair is positive, and they repel. Superb reasoning! Wow fact: lightning is static electricity on a giant scale, as ice bits rub together inside storm clouds. Challenge: rub a plastic comb on dry hair and hold it near tiny bits of paper. What happens?

faq.q: What moves when you charge something by rubbing?
faq.a: Only electrons move. They are negative, so whatever gains electrons becomes negative, and whatever loses them becomes positive.
asks: Do protons move in static electricity?

faq.a: Positive and negative charges pull on each other with an electric force. Like charges push each other away.
Static electricity is electric charge that builds up on the surface of an object and stays there instead of flowing.

faq.q: Why does my hair stand up after rubbing a balloon?
faq.a: Each hair loses electrons and becomes positive. The hairs repel each other and are attracted to the negative balloon.
asks: Why does static make hair stand up?

faq.q: Why do I get a shock from a door handle?
faq.a: Walking on carpet can charge your body. When you touch metal, the extra charge jumps across suddenly as a tiny spark.

facts: When objects are charged by friction, only electrons are transferred.
Like charges repel and opposite charges attract.
